History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Young woman with acute left-sided throbbing headache preceded by visual aura, associated photophobia, nausea, and two episodes of vomiting; clinical impression is migraine with aura.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Terrible” left-sided headache beginning around midday today.  
• Onset/duration: Sudden awareness today; similar episode a few weeks ago that lasted ~2 days.  
• Character: Throbbing pain, localized to left side; worsens when leaning forward or moving head/neck.  
• Aura: Zig-zag lines and blurred vision in both eyes minutes before pain onset.  
• Associated symptoms: Photophobia (wearing sunglasses), nausea, 2× vomiting.  
• Pertinent negatives: No fever, rash, speech difficulty, limb weakness, balance problems, head trauma, or breathlessness.  
• Patient concerns: Fear of brain cancer due to friend’s recent bereavement.

Past Medical History:
• Denies chronic illnesses; never previously diagnosed with migraine.  

Medications:
• Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive pill) – dose/route/frequency not documented (started 3 months ago).  
Allergies: Not recorded.

Social History:
• Occupation: Fashion industry; currently experiencing high job stress.  
• Lives alone.  
• Smoking: Denies.  
• Alcohol: Denies.  
• Exercise: None reported.

Family History:
• Mother: Migraine; hypothyroidism.  
• No known family brain tumours.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• General/neurologic exam findings: Not recorded (clinician verbal ROS negative for focal deficits).  

Investigations:
• None performed or ordered during visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Acute migraine with visual aura most consistent with presentation.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Migraine with aura – unilateral throbbing, visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, positive family history; no focal deficits.  
2. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) – positional headache and recent estrogen OCP use support; lack of focal signs or progressive course opposes.  
3. Intracranial mass/tumour – headache with vomiting and positional component; acute onset and normal neurologic review argue against.

Issue 1: Acute migraine with aura  
• Provide symptomatic relief: recommend Paracetamol or Co-codamol and an NSAID (Ibuprofen or Naproxen).  
• Advise rest in dark, quiet room.  
• Initiate headache diary to identify triggers and frequency.  
• Discuss prophylactic therapy if attacks become frequent; review next week.

Issue 2: Rule-out secondary headache causes  
• Educate on red-flag symptoms (worsening headache, lack of response to meds, new neurologic deficits, vision changes, escalating neck pain).  
• Instruct to seek urgent review or emergency care if red-flags occur.  
• Consider neuro-imaging / further work-up if headache pattern changes or fails to respond to therapy (e.g., to exclude CVST or space-occupying lesion).

Issue 3: Contraceptive counselling and thrombosis risk  
• Note estrogen-containing OCP is a thrombotic risk factor; discuss at follow-up whether alternative contraception warranted if headaches recur or if CVST risk becomes a concern.

General plan items:  
• Follow-up appointment in 1 week or sooner if symptoms persist/worsen.  
• Encourage stress-management strategies and regular physical activity.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No documented vitals, physical examination details, or allergy status – should be obtained at next contact.  
● No transcript/DDx conflicts identified.  
● Transcript clarity good; no major inaudible sections.
